subject.title: fix(cron): keep no-channel implicit cron runs successful instead of failing delivery (#56078)

question: Should implicit no-channel announce-to-last cron delivery be recorded as ok/not-delivered instead of error, while explicit or channel-resolved delivery failures remain fail-closed?
rationale: The patch is narrow and source-backed, but it changes persisted cron status, retry/backoff, and alert behavior for an existing requested-delivery route class, and contributor proof is still below the full user path previously requested.

options.title: Require Proof Then Merge
options.body: Ask for redacted cron add/run or equivalent loopback gateway proof plus docs alignment, then accept the narrow ok/not-delivered semantics.

options.title: Override Proof Now
options.body: A maintainer can accept the dispatcher/test evidence as sufficient and own the remaining end-to-end proof risk.

options.title: Defer To Warning Model
options.body: Pause or close this branch if maintainers want the broader first-class warning status direction instead of ok/not-delivered for this case.

recommendation.title: Require Proof Then Merge
recommendation.body: Ask for redacted cron add/run or equivalent loopback gateway proof plus docs alignment, then accept the narrow ok/not-delivered semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current history on the cron delivery target, dispatch, gateway command-cron, and status-boundary paths touched by this semantic change.
